figures.finding: No collective agreement or statutory minimum sets a Nigerian actor's pay: the Actors Guild of Nigeria's president said in August 2026 that the guild still needs an Act of the National Assembly to create the legal foundation for minimum remuneration standards and standard contracts.

sources.said: According to the national president, AGN needs legislative backing to institutionalise standard contractual frameworks, protect actors from exploitation, and legally enforce a structured regulatory environment across Nollywood. … “It will promote dignity in our work, and create the legal foundation for minimum remuneration standards, professional contracts, better working conditions, and stronger protection of actors’ rights and intellectual contributions.

He said a formal legislation passed by the National Assembly would guarantee actors access to standard contracts, intellectual property protections, royalties, and residual payments for their distributed works.
“You see big names when they fall sick, they don’t get any help because their financial remuneration from the work they do does not extend to royalties and residuals,” the AGN president noted.

figures.finding: Screen actors' body is the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), organised in state chapters: new members train at their chapter and pass an annual induction before receiving an ID card, members who skip revalidation are struck off, and licensing of actors is not yet mandatory (the guild wants legislation to introduce it). The last published registration fee found is N5,000, set by the national president in March 2013 (down from N15,000 to N20,000).

figures.finding: Stage practitioners' umbrella body is the National Association of Nigerian Theatre Arts Practitioners (NANTAP): Full Membership is a ₦50,000 registration with five years' proven performance credits, Student Membership ₦10,000, State Membership ₦10,000 a year, Fellowship ₦50,000 with fifteen years' credits.

figures.finding: Most films are made in English, then Igbo and Yoruba: of 304 films the censors' board classified from January to April 2026, 201 were in English, 44 in Igbo, 42 in Yoruba, 9 in Hindi, 5 in Hausa and 3 in Bini.
figures.applies: Nigeria, films classified by the NFVCB, January to April 2026.

sources.said: The language distribution of the 304 films classified during the review period shows English language productions leading with 201 films, followed by Igbo with 44 films, Yoruba with 42, Hindi with 9, Hausa with 5 and Bini with 3.

figures.finding: Lagos is where the most films are made (234 in the second quarter of 2021), ahead of Abuja (196) and Onitsha (174).
figures.applies: Nigeria, Nollywood film production by location, April to June 2021.
